hypothesis: At contest cost 1, denial still dominates: on the fresh holdout rivals challenged 99.0% of claims and canceled 2436 of 2503 (97.3%), so 57.3% of games drew with a 40-round median. One Prestige is too cheap next to the value of blocking a rival's win, so contesting stays a reflex instead of a decision. Set the contest cost to 2. That equals the full support price of a claim (2 factions at support cost 1), so one contest costs the rival as much Prestige as the claimant spent to set up the claim. Contests become income-limited choices: a rival blocks only when it can pay and when blocking beats its own plans. The claimant gains a real timing choice — bait contests to drain rivals, then claim when rivals cannot pay. Cycle 1 predicted cost 1 would do this; the holdout shows the threshold was set too low, so this tests the next step of the same mechanism.
prediction: Challenged fraction falls from 0.990 to roughly 0.4–0.8 on screen and the new holdout, because contests become Prestige-limited. Canceled claims divided by total claims falls well below 0.97. Draws fall on both seed sets: holdout far below 0.573 and screen at or below 0.031. Median rounds fall, with holdout clearly below 40. Claims completed per game rise. Wins stay spread: at least three profiles each win at least 10% of finished games, so no collapse to one winning profile. Average Prestige spent on contests per game falls even at double unit cost, showing rivals decline some contests rather than pay.
refutation_evidence: Any of these results count against the change: draws rise, or holdout draws stay above roughly 0.3; median rounds rise; challenged fraction stays near 0.99, meaning cost is not the lever and denial is still effectively free; challenged fraction collapses below roughly 0.15 while one profile (for example early_support) takes a dominant win share, showing lost counterplay; counterleader or prestige_farmer wins fall to near zero. A sharp screen-versus-holdout split, like the incumbent's 0.031 versus 0.573, marks the candidate as seed-fragile; retain the incumbent and record the tradeoff for human review.
